# Smithers documentation (full)

# Welcome to Smithers
https://smithers.sh/docs/

Smithers maintains your codebase. It turns issues into reviewed, tested changes and keeps the project wiki current. Flows beside your code define how.

[Open Smithers](https://smithers.sh/smithersai/smithers)
[Follow the quickstart](/docs/quickstart/)

![The Smithers home: the question What should we work on?, the chat box, and four tiles: Fix an issue, Review a PR, Ask the codebase, and Run it every night.](/images/app/home.png)

Smithers home.

## Register your repository

**Planned.** Paste a link to an open-source repository. Smithers analyzes it while you watch: license, checks, commits, contributors, agent readiness, and how much faster its CI could run. Then we review it and set Smithers up for it.

[Register a repository](https://smithers.sh/?register=1)

![Registering github.com/acme/widgets: Smithers has chosen the license, checks, contribution style, and a workflow to build; cards show commits with agent-assisted work, contributors, agent readiness 72, a CI estimate of 14 to 3 minutes, and cleanups 18 of 100.](/images/app/register.png)

Registration on main, with example data. Planned for smithers.sh.

You can register one repository at a time.

# Quickstart
https://smithers.sh/docs/quickstart/

Open [Smithers](https://smithers.sh/smithersai/smithers) in your browser. You do not need the CLI to use the app. Available actions depend on sign-in, repository permissions, and the services enabled by your host.

## 1. Connect your account

Select **Connect GitHub** or **Sign in with GitHub**, review the requested permissions, and return to Smithers. Select **Start Automating** when your workspace is ready.

The setup checklist follows three steps: **Connect GitHub**, **Add a repository**, and **Set up a job**.

## 2. Choose a repository

Select **Add a repository** and follow the import flow, or open a repository already available to your account. Check the selected owner and repository before requesting work.

Open **Chat** with Command-K on macOS or Control-K on Windows and Linux. Read the selected repository's instructions with:

```text
/files.read CONTRIBUTING.md
```

A file card opens in the conversation. Use **Maximize card** for more room. If the repository has no contribution guide, open `/files.read README.md` instead.

For search, type `?` in Chat to choose a search type. Type `/` to browse commands and repository flows.

## 3. Ask a bounded question

Try a read-only request:

```text
Explain this repository. Which files should I read before making a small
documentation change? Do not modify files or start a flow.
```

Read the response and inspect the referenced files. Complete any access step the app requests. [Sign in](/docs/learn/account/) covers access; [Work in a box](/docs/learn/boxes/) covers boxes.

## 4. Set up a job

Select **Set up a job**, or a recommended repository job. Review its configuration and proposed plan before approving registration. Follow the run card and background toast until registration finishes.

The repository's job buttons remain available after setup and show their current state. Use [Dispatcher](/docs/learn/agent-and-trigger/#put-it-on-a-schedule) to inspect declarations and live registrations, prepare a schedule, or run an enabled registration now.

## 5. Make and inspect a change

Choose a small issue and state the expected result and checks. For example:

```text
Update the contribution guide's stale setup instruction to match the current
package scripts. Run the documentation checks and show me the diff.
```

Chat stays usable while work runs. Use **Steer** on the run for a correction. During the current chat turn, Enter steers and Alt-Enter queues a follow-up.

Read the resulting Change's **Diff**, **Checks**, and **Review**. Select **Land**. On repositories that send work upstream, such as Smithers, the owner merges the pull request. [History](/docs/learn/issue-to-main/) (`/history.show`) shows each issue's path to main.

## Continue

  - [Run a flow](/docs/learn/run-a-flow/): Choose a flow and provide its inputs.
  - [Inspect a run](/docs/learn/watch-an-agent/): Read its trace, steer, or stop work.
  - [Review a change](/docs/learn/review-a-change/): Check the diff and evidence before landing.
  - [Troubleshoot the app](/docs/learn/troubleshooting/): Resolve access, box, and run problems.

Prefer a terminal? Follow the [CLI quickstart](/docs/cli-quickstart/).

---

# Pricing
https://smithers.sh/docs/pricing/

Smithers picks and runs the models. Model usage draws on your account credit. New accounts start with $10 of credit.

## Plans

| | Free | Pro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Price | $0 | $50 per month |
| Model credit | $10 once, at signup | $50 per month |
| Running sandboxes | 1 | 3 |
| Idle sleep | 30 minutes | 1 hour |
| Sandbox-hours per day | 4 | Unlimited |

Pro's monthly credit is added when each monthly payment succeeds and expires at the end of that month; unused credit does not roll over. A refund or cancellation ends it. The plans card shows the credit you have left, the credit your plan includes, and the date the next credit arrives.

When credit runs out, new model calls stop until more credit arrives. The plans card then offers Upgrade to Pro.

Sandbox-hours measure the time your sandboxes are awake, added together across running sandboxes. Daily usage resets at midnight UTC.

Pro renews monthly until you cancel. Cancel anytime in the billing portal; Pro stays active until the end of the paid month. See [Terms](/terms/), [Refunds](/refunds/) and [Privacy](/privacy/).

## Choose or manage a plan

Sign in to [Smithers](https://smithers.sh/smithersai/smithers) and run `/billing.plans` to see your current plan, credit, sandbox usage, and upgrades in the conversation. `/billing.portal` opens subscription management when billing is available.

Checkout is not open yet on deployments where payments are disabled. The plans card shows availability before you choose an upgrade.

## Open-source tools

The CLI and libraries are MIT-licensed, with no Smithers license fee. Run them in your own environment and pay your providers for model usage and infrastructure.

See [CLI and libraries](/docs/developers/) for setup and supported platforms.

# Self-host Smithers
https://smithers.sh/docs/self-hosting/

Smithers runs as one unprivileged container, next to a PostgreSQL 18 database you provide, with one persistent volume. One machine, one owner, local disk.

**Partly available.** The image is not published yet ([#1667](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1667)). Build it from a source checkout:

```sh
docker build -f distribution/Dockerfile -t smithers .
```

## Start it

```sh
umask 077
cat >smithers.env <<EOF
DATABASE_URL=postgres://smithers:replace-me@postgres:5432/smithers?sslmode=require
SMITHERS_AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
EOF
docker run --name smithers --restart unless-stopped -p 4000:4000 \
  --network smithers \
  --env-file ./smithers.env \
  -v smithers-data:/var/lib/smithers \
  smithers
```

`--network` must reach PostgreSQL. The app listens on port 4000 (set `PORT` to change it). The bootstrap token is needed only until the first owner account exists; then remove it from `smithers.env`.

## Give it model keys

Put provider keys in a JSON file on the data volume and point `SMITHERS_PLATFORM_MODEL_KEYS_FILE` at it. Providers: `anthropic`, `openai`, `cerebras`, `openrouter`, and `vercel` (the AI Gateway key). Every call is metered against the owner's credit; grant it with `smithers-backend credits grant`.

## Back up and upgrade

Stop the container, then run the image's `backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, or `upgrade.sh` entrypoint against the same volume. Upgrade always starts from a verified backup.

## More

[The distribution guide](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/blob/main/distribution/README.md) has every variable and command: Railway, the macOS app with its own PostgreSQL, microVM isolation, subscription connections, backup, restore, and upgrade.

# CLI and libraries
https://smithers.sh/docs/developers/

Use the CLI to author and run flows in your own repository. Use the TypeScript libraries when you need to define actions, build targets, and execution rules in code.

For the hosted application, start with the [app quickstart](/docs/quickstart/).

## Get started from the terminal

The 1.0 release candidate is not on npm. Install it from the source checkout.

[Install the CLI](/docs/installation/)
[Read the CLI quickstart](/docs/cli-quickstart/)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/smithersai/smithers.git
cd smithers
pnpm install
cargo build --locked --release -p smithers-ffi --bin smithers-jj-export
export PATH="$PWD/node_modules/.bin:$PATH"
```

From your project directory, scaffold a flow, edit its instructions, and configure the credential its `model:` field requires before running it:

```bash
smthrs init change
smthrs flow start change
```

That creates `flows/change/flow.mdx`, a flow that lives with your code, and runs it. The [CLI quickstart](/docs/cli-quickstart/) walks through the same steps with what to expect at each one.

## Explore the build graph

A workspace contains packages and their build targets. Select a file to inspect the workspace configuration or a package's test and review targets.

<HeroStage />

![Build targets form a dependency graph, and an edit re-runs only the steps it makes stale while the rest comes from cache.](/images/build-graph.gif)

## Supported platforms

The release candidate's required platform is Linux with Node 26.4.0. See the [support matrix](/docs/reference/support-matrix/).

## Go deeper

  - [Your first flow](/docs/tutorials/first-flow/): Build a typed flow from actions and run it durably.
  - [Markdown flows](/docs/guides/markdown-flows/): Define a flow's instructions, capabilities, and budget.
  - [CLI reference](/docs/reference/cli/): Look up commands, inputs, and outputs.

# Installation
https://smithers.sh/docs/installation/

## Requirements

- Node.js <code>>=26.4.0</code>, or Bun 1.4 or later. See the [support matrix](/docs/reference/support-matrix/).
- pnpm 11.25.0, Git, and the Rust toolchain `rust-toolchain.toml` pins (`rustup toolchain install`).
- A model provider key, and `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` (Vercel AI Gateway) to run flows. See [environment variables](/docs/reference/environment-variables/#provider-keys).
- No database server. Run state is local SQLite in the project's `.flows/` directory.

See the [RC support matrix](/docs/reference/support-matrix/) for engine ranges, platforms, and hosting limits.

## Install the CLI

These docs describe <code>1.0.0-rc.1</code>. It is not published to npm: npm's `@smthrs/cli` is the 0.x line. Install it from the source checkout:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/smithersai/smithers.git
cd smithers
pnpm install
cargo build --locked --release -p smithers-ffi --bin smithers-jj-export
export PATH="$PWD/node_modules/.bin:$PATH"
smthrs --version
```

`smthrs --version` prints <code>1.0.0-rc.1</code>. The `cargo` line builds the filesystem helper flow commands require. The PATH line puts this checkout's `smthrs` (and its alias `smithers`) on the current shell. Change to your own project directory before running `smthrs init`. Target commands such as `smthrs build` and `smthrs test` run with this CLI in any directory; they load `WORKSPACE.ts` and `PACKAGE.ts` against the checkout's own Effect and Smithers packages.

:::caution[declaration_dependency_mismatch]
Target declarations and the CLI must resolve the same physical Effect and Smithers packages. A second, separately installed CLI fails with `declaration_dependency_mismatch` even when its versions match. Use one CLI.
:::

## Use the libraries

The `@smthrs/*` libraries are not on npm either. Link a project directory to the checkout's `examples` workspace, which carries the packages the tutorials and guides import, and the one pinned Effect (<code>4.0.0-rc.115</code>):

```bash
mkdir my-flows && cd my-flows
echo '{ "type": "module" }' > package.json
ln -s /path/to/smithers/examples/node_modules node_modules
```

Run programs with `node <file>.ts`. A package that workspace lacks, such as `@smthrs/artifacts`, resolves only inside the checkout.

## Verify the install

```bash
smthrs doctor
```

`doctor` prints one line per check without running a flow, and exits 1 when any check fails:

- registry: the flows discovered under `flows/`.
- state and databases: `.flows/` and the migrations applied to `control.db` and `engine.db` ("not created yet" before first use).
- runtime: the Node.js version against the supported range.
- jj: whether the configured Jujutsu executable is available.
- providers: which provider credentials are set, and which are exported but empty.

## Stay current

```bash
git pull
pnpm install
cargo build --locked --release -p smithers-ffi --bin smithers-jj-export
```

`smthrs update` reads npm's dist-tags for `@smthrs/cli` and never installs anything.

## Next steps

  - [CLI quickstart](/docs/cli-quickstart/): Scaffold a flow and run it.
  - [CLI reference](/docs/reference/cli/): Every verb the smthrs command ships.

# CLI quickstart
https://smithers.sh/docs/cli-quickstart/

Create a flow that lives with your code, give it a small prompt, and inspect the result. To use the hosted app instead, follow the [app quickstart](/docs/quickstart/).

## 1. Install the CLI

Use Node.js 26.4.0 or later. You also need a provider credential for the model that will run the flow, and `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` (a Vercel AI Gateway key): Smithers asks Jev to judge every completion, and `smthrs flow start` refuses to run without it.

The 1.0 release candidate is not published to npm yet. Follow the [source-checkout installation](/docs/installation/#install-the-cli), including its PATH setting, then verify:

```bash
smthrs --version
```

The version should start with `1.0.`.

## 2. Scaffold a flow

From the project directory where you want the agent to work, run:

```bash
smthrs init change
```

In a new workspace, this creates:

- package.json
- WORKSPACE.ts
- PACKAGE.ts
- flows/
  - change/
    - flow.mdx
- .flows/

Existing declarations and flow files are retained. In a Git or jj repository, the command adds `.flows/` to `.gitignore`. Execution databases are created when a runtime command needs them.

For an npm workspace, or a flow without build declarations, see the [init reference](/docs/reference/cli/init/).

## 3. Give it a prompt and a model

Open `flows/change/flow.mdx`. Keep the frontmatter, then replace the starter body with a small, concrete prompt, for example:

```md
Read the project's README and package manifest. Explain how to run its tests
and name the source directories a new contributor should read first.
Do not modify files or run commands.
```

The `model:` field selects the provider and model. `init` chooses it from the first available provider credential; if none is set, the generated comment names the key required by its default model. Set that credential in your shell, or change `model:` to a model you can use. `init` tries `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, then `CEREBRAS_API_KEY`. A model call uses that provider's account and usage limits.

The starter declares file-read, file-write, and process-spawn capabilities for editing and testing. For this read-only prompt, replace its `capabilities:` line with `capabilities: ["fs:read:**"]`. Review that declaration whenever you change the prompt; the flow name comes from its directory, so no `name:` field is needed.

Check the configuration and flow discovery:

```bash
smthrs doctor
smthrs flow list
```

`doctor` reports runtime and configuration problems without running a flow. `flow list` should include `change` with the description from its frontmatter. Resolve any failing checks before launching.

## 4. Run and inspect it

```bash
smthrs flow start change
```

`flow start` plans the flow, grants its requested capabilities for this run, and launches it. Review the flow's instructions and capabilities before running it. The command stays attached until the run completes, fails, is cancelled, or waits for approval.

After it settles, list the runs and use the returned run id to inspect one:

```bash
smthrs runs list
smthrs runs show <run-id>
smthrs runs logs <run-id>
```

A successful run appears as `completed`. Its transcript should contain the test instructions and source-directory explanation you requested. If it fails, `runs show` explains the diagnosis and `runs logs` shows the transcript.

Smithers records completed action results in the project's journal. A resumed run can reuse those results; starting another `flow start` creates a new run. See [durable execution](/docs/concepts/durable-execution/) for what replay preserves.

## Next steps

  - [Your first flow](/docs/tutorials/first-flow/): Build a typed flow from actions and run it durably.
  - [Markdown flows](/docs/guides/markdown-flows/): Define the instructions, capabilities, and budget of a flow.mdx.
  - [MCP setup](/docs/guides/mcp-setup/): Give a run's agent access to MCP tools.

# How Smithers works
https://smithers.sh/docs/how-it-works/

Smithers is built from a few ideas.

| Idea | In one line |
| --- | --- |
| [Conversation](/docs/how-it-works/conversations/) | A chat with Smithers, or the discussion on an issue. |
| [Issue](/docs/how-it-works/issues/) | Something to get done, from open to verified. |
| [Wiki](/docs/how-it-works/wiki/) | What the project knows, versioned and kept current. |
| [Agent](/docs/how-it-works/agents/) | Instructions, a model, what it may do, and a budget. |
| [Trigger](/docs/how-it-works/triggers-and-flows/) | Something that happens: a message, a schedule, an issue or code event. |
| [Flow](/docs/how-it-works/triggers-and-flows/) | The steps Smithers runs when a trigger fires. |
| Run | One durable execution of a flow; it resumes after a restart. |

## How they fit

**How the pieces connect**

A trigger starts a flow. The flow puts agents to work. Agents reply in conversations, move issues forward, and update the wiki. Every step is recorded.

1. **Something happens.** A message arrives, a schedule comes due, or an issue is labeled.
2. **Its rule picks a flow.**
3. **The flow runs.** Each agent uses its own model, permissions, and budget.
4. **Work comes back.** Replies land in the conversation. Code changes arrive as pull requests. The wiki refreshes when code lands.

## Four ways in

Everything is meant to be reachable four ways. The tutorials show each one in a tab.

| Surface | For | Open it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GUI | People | The Smithers app |
| TUI | People | `smthrs tui` |
| CLI | Scripts and agents | `smthrs <command>` |
| API | Scripts and services | HTTP |

## Nothing is lost

Smithers records each step as it finishes. After a restart, a run picks up where it stopped without repeating finished work. [Durable execution](/docs/concepts/durable-execution/) explains the engine.

Smithers is in alpha. Each page marks its sections **Available now**, **Partly available**, or **Planned**.

---

# Conversations
https://smithers.sh/docs/how-it-works/conversations/

A **conversation** lasts: a subject, its messages, and the people and agents taking part. Work starts in a conversation and reports back to it.

| Kind | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| Chat | A private conversation with Smithers and your agents. |
| Issue discussion | Comments on an [issue](/docs/how-it-works/issues/), visible to the repository's team. |

## Chats

**Available now.** [Chat](/docs/learn/chat/) with Smithers in the app or the TUI. The app keeps your chats for your account; the TUI keeps conversations in the project.

**Partly available.** The API keeps private chats, searchable and syncable, with agents replying under their own names. The app's chat list is planned ([#2111](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2111)).

## Issue discussions

**Available now.** Every issue has comments, and every change to it is recorded. The list shows the repository's Smithers issues with its GitHub issues.

## Messages start work

A message can trigger a flow. The assistant answers, or hands the request to the right [agent](/docs/how-it-works/agents/) and posts its reply in the same conversation.

**Planned.** Message triggers for chats. See [Triggers and flows](/docs/how-it-works/triggers-and-flows/).

## Sync with Slack and Telegram

A conversation can sync with one Slack thread or Telegram chat. Sync is two-way: a message, edit, or delete on either side appears once on the other. Agents post under their own names.

**Partly available.** The API connects a conversation; setup in the app is planned ([#2116](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2116)), and live acceptance is tracked in [#2105](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2105)). Telegram reactions are not synced ([#2110](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2110)). See [Sync a conversation](/docs/learn/sync-a-conversation/).

## Next

- [Issues](/docs/how-it-works/issues/): work to get done.
- [Chat with an agent](/docs/learn/chat/): the first tutorial.

# Issues
https://smithers.sh/docs/how-it-works/issues/

An **issue** is something to get done. Discussion happens in its comments.

## States

```text
open → fixed → verified → closed
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| State | `open`, `fixed`, `verified`, or `closed`. |
| Fixed by | Who marked it fixed. |
| Verified by | Who confirmed the fix. Never the fixer. |
| Assignees, labels, milestone | Who owns it and how it is grouped. |

**Available now.** The issue card has **Fixed**, **Verify**, **Close**, and **Reopen**; `/issues.fix 42` and `/issues.verify 42` do the same, and so does the API.

**Planned.** Owner, due date, priority, and parent issue ([#2112](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2112)).

## Let Smithers fix it

**Available now.** Label an issue `smithers`, or run `/issue.implement 42` in the app. Smithers plans the change, runs the checks, and opens a pull request. **History** (`/history.show`) shows where each issue is.

## Sync with Linear

**Partly available.** A repository can sync issues and comments with a Linear team, both ways. The host must enable integrations; the app has no setup screen yet ([#2116](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2116)).

## Next

- [Create an issue](/docs/learn/create-an-issue/): step by step.
- [Agents](/docs/how-it-works/agents/): who works on issues.

# Wiki
https://smithers.sh/docs/how-it-works/wiki/

The **wiki** is what people and agents know about a repository. Both read it and write it. Agents read it before they plan.

## One wiki, two parts

**Available now.** Each repository has one wiki with a **public** part and a **private** part. The public part is readable by anyone who can read the repository. The private part is for people with explicit access to it. A page stays in the part it was written in.

## Shaped like a vault

**Available now.** Pages are Markdown files in folders, like an Obsidian vault. `[[Page]]` links another page, `[[Page#Heading|label]]` a heading, and `![[assets/logo.png]]` embeds a file. Every page shows what links to it. Front matter, tags, and aliases are kept as written.

## Versioned

**Available now.** Every edit, rename, and delete is a revision; earlier revisions stay readable, even after a delete. Edits never silently overwrite each other.

## Kept current

When a change lands, Smithers regenerates the pages it affects, reviews each against the code, and publishes it. Pages a person edited stay as written.

**Partly available.** Refresh runs when main moves, for repositories with the stack on and a declared wiki. Hosted proof is tracked in [#1923](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1923).

## Sync with Notion and Obsidian

**Planned.** Two-way sync with Notion and with a local Obsidian folder ([#2122](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2122)).

## Next

- [Use the wiki](/docs/learn/wiki/): step by step.
- [Agents](/docs/how-it-works/agents/): who reads it.

---

# Agents
https://smithers.sh/docs/how-it-works/agents/

An **agent** is a file in your repository: `flows/<id>/flow.mdx`, or `flows/<id>/SKILL.md`. An agent is a flow, so everything that runs flows runs agents. The front matter sets the model, what the agent may do, and its budget. The body is its instructions.

## Write one

**Available now.**

```markdown title="flows/reviewer/flow.mdx"
---
description: Reviews a change and returns a verdict with reasons.
model: [sol, opus]
effort: high
capabilities: ["fs:read:**", "proc:spawn:*"]
budget:
  tokens: 200000
  milliseconds: 600000
---

# Review the change

Read the diff. Run the tests. Return approve or request changes,
with the evidence for each finding.
```

| Key | What it decides |
| --- | --- |
| `description` | One line shown wherever the agent is listed. |
| `model` | The model: an alias such as `sol`, `astra`, `luna`, `opus`, `fable`, or `qwen`, or `provider:modelId`. A list is a primary and fallbacks. |
| `effort` | Reasoning effort, such as `low` or `high`. |
| `capabilities` | What it may do. Anything else is refused. |
| `budget` | The most tokens and time one run may spend. |
| `flows` | Other agents or flows it may call. |
| `disable-model-invocation` | `true` lets people start it but not other agents. |
| Body | The instructions: the job, the output, and when to stop and ask. |

Skills are `SKILL.md` files beside your flows. A skill adds instructions, never permissions. [flow.mdx frontmatter](/docs/reference/flow-mdx/) lists every key.

## Start one

**GUI**

**Available now.** Type `/` and the agent's name, or ask for it in chat. See [Run a flow](/docs/learn/run-a-flow/).

**TUI**

**Available now.** `/agent` opens a picker. `/agent reviewer` fills in the composer; `/agent reviewer Review math.js` starts it in the background right away.

![Starting a custom review agent from the TUI.](/images/learn/tui-custom-agent.gif)

The TUI with a fixture agent.

**CLI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs flow start reviewer --data '{"args":"Review the working copy"}'
```

**API**

**Available now.** `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/invoke` with `{"flow":"reviewer","input":{"args":"..."}}`.

The model is chosen in order: the one you asked for, then the file's `model`, then the default.

## If it won't start

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `unknown_agent` | No agent has that name. |
| `not_an_agent` | It's a `flow.ts` flow; run it as a flow. |
| `not_invocable` | Another agent tried to start a people-only agent. |
| `unreadable` | Its instructions couldn't be read. Fix the file and retry. |
| `unknown_seat` | `model` names no known provider or alias. |
| `unknown_effort` | `effort` isn't a supported level. |

## Agents call agents

**Available now.** An agent lists what it may call under `flows`. Each call is its own run, with its own model, permissions, and timeline. A called agent can only do less than its caller, never more.

## See what an agent did

**Available now.** Filter the run list by the agent's id, then open a run's timeline. See [Watch an agent work](/docs/learn/watch-an-agent/).

**Partly available.** **Agents** in the app lists the built-in agents with a **Runs** button each; your own agents join the list with [#2113](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2113).

## Budgets

**Available now.** `budget` caps a run's tokens and time.

**Planned.** When a run hits its budget or time limit, it pauses and asks you to continue or stop ([#2114](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2114)).

## Memory

**Partly available.** Add a memory bank to `capabilities`, such as `memory:read:global-team` and `memory:write:global-team`. The agent then recalls what's relevant from that bank as it works, and can save what it learns. Agents share a bank only when each is allowed it. See [Memory](/docs/concepts/memory/).

## Next

- [Configure an agent and a trigger](/docs/learn/agent-and-trigger/): put it on a schedule.
- [Triggers and flows](/docs/how-it-works/triggers-and-flows/): what starts an agent.

# Triggers and flows
https://smithers.sh/docs/how-it-works/triggers-and-flows/

A **trigger** is something that happens. A **flow** is the steps Smithers runs when it does. A **rule** connects them.

## Kinds of trigger

| Trigger | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schedule | Every weekday at 9:00, run the review. | Available now |
| Issue event | An issue is labeled `smithers`, or gets a comment. | Partly available |
| Code event | A change opens, lands, or main moves. | Partly available |
| Message | A message arrives in a chat. | Planned |
| Manual | You run a registered rule now. | Available now |

## Flows

A flow lives at `flows/<name>/`: a `flow.mdx` whose body is the prompt, or a `flow.ts`. Each execution is a run. Every step is recorded as it finishes, so a stopped run resumes without redoing work. [Agents](/docs/how-it-works/agents/) are flows too.

**Available now.** Run flows from the app's `/` menu, the TUI's `/flow`, `smthrs flow start`, or the API. See [Flows, actions, and plans](/docs/concepts/flows-actions-plans/).

## Rules

A repository declares its rules in `.smithers/FACTORY.ts`, under `on`. The key is the trigger; the value names the flow.

```ts title=".smithers/FACTORY.ts"
import { Smithers as S } from "@smthrs/targets"

export const factory = S.Factory({
  summary: "How this repository develops itself.",
  on: {
    "issue.labeled:smithers": { flow: "implement", description: "Implement an issue labeled smithers" },
    "change.opened": { flow: "review", description: "Review every change" },
    "schedule:0 9 * * 1-5": { flow: "review", description: "Weekday morning review of main" }
  }
})
```

The app's **Dispatcher** lists each rule as declared.

**Partly available.** When main moves, rules for `flow.mdx` flows go live: schedules, and issue, comment, pull request, and push events. Rules for `flow.ts` flows stay declared only. Smithers also runs its built-in rules: fixing issues labeled `smithers`, and refreshing history and the wiki when code lands.

**Available now.** Schedules register directly: in the app with **Dispatcher**, **Register a rule**, or for a local project with `smthrs triggers register`. See [Configure an agent and a trigger](/docs/learn/agent-and-trigger/).

**Planned.** Message rules, so a chat message starts the assistant.

## Once only

A repeated event never runs twice.

## Next

- [How Smithers works](/docs/how-it-works/): the whole picture.
- [Watch an agent work](/docs/learn/watch-an-agent/): follow a run.

# Chat with an agent
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/chat/

Ask for something concrete. Smithers answers in the conversation. Slow work runs in the background, so you can keep chatting.

## Send a message

**GUI**

**Available now.**

1. Check the repository name beside the message box.
2. Select **Chat**, or press Command-K (Ctrl-K on Windows and Linux).
3. Say what you want and how you'll judge the result. Press Enter.

![Opening Chat, typing a question, and reading the reply in the Smithers app.](/images/learn/app-chat.gif)

Chat in the app, with a scripted reply.

Smithers answers in prose, shows a card, or starts a flow. If a step needs sign-in, it asks in the conversation.

**TUI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs tui
```

Type your request and press Enter. Shift+Enter or Ctrl+J adds a line; Up and Down recall earlier prompts; Ctrl+G opens your editor for a long one. Type `@` to mention a file.

New to the TUI? Start with [Smithers in your terminal](/docs/tui/).

![Writing a two-line request in the TUI and reading the answer.](/images/learn/tui-composer.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

**CLI**

**Available now.** Answer one prompt and exit:

```sh
smthrs tui -p "Explain this repository. Which files should I read first?"
```

The answer prints to standard output. Add `--model provider:model` to pick the model.

**API**

**Partly available.** Create a private chat, then post messages as comments. An agent reply to a chat message is planned.

```sh
curl -X POST "$SMITHERS_API/api/repos/acme/app/issues" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMITHERS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Conversation","kind":"chat","idempotency_key":"chat-1"}'
```

The app's own chat route, `POST /api/agent/turn`, needs a signed-in browser session.

## Use cards and commands

Results arrive as cards beside the request: a file, a run, an approval. Select **Maximize card** for more room.

**GUI**

**Available now.** Type `/` to browse commands and flows. A trailing dot, such as `/review.`, lists a command group.

![The slash menu shows the repository review flow and the Review command group.](/images/app/slash.png)

The command menu.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Type `/` to browse commands. Repository flows appear in the same menu.

**CLI**

**Available now.** `smthrs --help` lists commands; add `--help` to any command.

**API**

**Available now.** See [HTTP and RPC endpoints](/docs/reference/http-api/).

## Steer or queue while it works

A turn can take a while. You don't have to wait.

- **Steer**: change the current request before its next step.
- **Queue**: add a follow-up that starts after this one.
- **Stop**: end the current turn and keep your draft.

**GUI**

**Available now.** While Smithers is answering, Enter steers and Alt+Enter queues. Queued messages stay with the conversation; you can edit or remove them. To correct a specific run, use **Steer** on its card.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Enter steers, Alt+Enter queues, Alt+Up brings queued messages back, and Esc stops the turn and returns queued messages to the editor. Esc leaves background workers running.

![Queueing a follow-up in the TUI, bringing it back to the editor, and stopping the turn.](/images/learn/tui-queue.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

**CLI**

**Available now** for durable runs, by run ID:

```sh
smthrs runs steer <run> --message "Keep the public API unchanged."
```

`smthrs runs cancel <run>` stops a run.

**API**

**Available now** for durable runs, over the API: `Steer { runId, message, idempotencyKey }` and `Cancel { runId, idempotencyKey }`. See [HTTP and RPC endpoints](/docs/reference/http-api/).

## Run a shell command

**GUI**

**Available now** in a [box](/docs/learn/boxes/): open its terminal from the box card.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Start a line with `!` to run a command and add its output to the conversation, or `!!` to keep the output out. Esc cancels it.

![Running a shell command from the TUI composer and adding its output to the conversation.](/images/learn/tui-shell-context.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

**CLI**

Use your shell.

**API**

**Available now.** A box's terminal is a WebSocket; see [Work in a box](/docs/learn/boxes/).

## Pick up where you left off

Conversations are saved. Come back to one, or branch from an earlier message to try another way.

**GUI**

**Available now.** The app keeps your conversation for your account. Reload and it's there.

**TUI**

**Available now.**

| Do | How |
| --- | --- |
| Continue the latest | `smthrs tui -c` |
| Pick one | `smthrs tui -r`, `/resume`, or Ctrl+K then `conversation:` |
| Name it | `/name <name>` |
| Branch from an earlier message | `/fork`; the original stays |
| Drop old context | `/compact` |
| Copy the last answer | `/copy` |

Running work restarts from its recorded steps. `/fork` doesn't change files; press `u` in **Summary** to [undo an edit](/docs/learn/review-a-change/).

![Forking a TUI conversation from an earlier message.](/images/learn/tui-fork-session.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

**CLI**

**Available now** for durable runs: `smthrs runs list`, then `smthrs runs resume <run>`.

**API**

**Available now** for durable runs: the `Resume` procedure.

# Sync a conversation with Slack or Telegram
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/sync-a-conversation/

**Partly available.** The API connects a conversation to Slack or Telegram. App setup is planned, and live acceptance is tracked in [#2105](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2105).

A conversation syncs with one Slack thread or one Telegram chat or topic. A message, edit, or delete on either side appears once on the other. Agents post under their own names.

| | Slack | Telegram |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Messages and replies | Both ways | Both ways |
| Edits | Both ways | Both ways |
| Deletes | Both ways | Smithers to Telegram only |
| Reactions | Both ways | Not synced ([#2110](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2110)) |

## Connect a conversation

**GUI**

**Planned.** Slack and Telegram rows on the Connect card ([#2116](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2116)).

![Design preview of the Connect card with Slack, Linear, and Notion rows.](/images/learn/preview-integrations.png)

Design preview with example data. Not connected yet.

**TUI**

**Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now** in the backend; live acceptance in [#2105](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2105). One route connects a conversation (an issue number):

```sh
curl -X PUT "$SMITHERS_API/api/repos/acme/app/issues/42/sync" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMITHERS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"provider":"slack","connection_id":"slack-main","scope_id":"T0123","conversation_id":"C0123","thread_id":""}'
```

An empty `thread_id` starts a new Slack thread. For Telegram, `scope_id` is the bot ID and `conversation_id` the chat ID. `GET` on the same route returns the mapping and its state. A mapping cannot change once set.

## See it synced

**GUI**

**Planned.** The conversation shows each message with its author, a `slack` mark on synced ones, and **Retry** on a message that did not deliver ([#2111](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2111)).

![Design preview of a chat: messages from a person and two agents, a Slack link, reactions, and a failed message with Retry.](/images/learn/preview-chat.png)

Design preview with example data. Not connected yet.

**TUI**

**Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now** in the backend. Synced messages are ordinary comments: `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/42/comments`. `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/state-events/stream` streams new ones.

# Create an issue
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/create-an-issue/

An issue is something to get done. It moves `open → fixed → verified → closed`. The person who verifies it cannot be the one who fixed it.

## Open the issue

**GUI**

**Available now.** Enter `/issues.create` and give it a title. `/issues.list` shows open issues; `/issues.view 42` opens one; `/issues.comment` replies.

**TUI**

**Planned.** Issue commands in the TUI ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned.** Issue commands in `smthrs` ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.**

```sh
curl -X POST "$SMITHERS_API/api/repos/acme/app/issues" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMITHERS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Footer link is hard to find","body":"Make the label clearer."}'
```

Set `SMITHERS_API` to your Smithers API origin and `SMITHERS_TOKEN` to a personal access token with the `write:repository` scope. The response is the issue, with its `number`.

## Hand it to the factory

**GUI**

**Available now.** Enter `/issue.implement 42`. The factory plans, changes, checks, and opens a pull request. **History** (`/history.show`) shows its progress.

**TUI**

**Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** Label the issue `smithers`:

```sh
curl -X PATCH "$SMITHERS_API/api/repos/acme/app/issues/42" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMITHERS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"labels":["smithers"]}'
```

## Mark it fixed, then verified

**GUI**

**Available now.** On the issue card, select **Fixed**, then, as someone else, **Verify**. Or enter `/issues.fix 42` and `/issues.verify 42`. **Planned:** owner, due date, and priority ([#2112](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2112)).

![Design preview of the issue list with filters and rows showing state and priority.](/images/learn/preview-issues.png)

Design preview with example data. Not connected yet.

**TUI**

**Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** Set `state` to `fixed`, then, as a different person, `verified`:

```sh
curl -X PATCH "$SMITHERS_API/api/repos/acme/app/issues/42" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMITHERS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"state":"verified"}'
```

Verifying your own fix fails with `self_verification`. Verifying an issue that is not `fixed` fails with `invalid_transition`.

# Follow an issue to main
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/issue-to-main/

When Smithers works on issues, each one moves through a path: planned, built, checked, opened as a pull request, landed. **History** shows every issue on that path at once, above the changes already on main.

## Turn it on

**GUI**

**Available now.** Select **History**, then **Bootstrap**. Smithers builds the history from main in the background; a toast follows it until it's ready. Needs admin permission on the repository.

**TUI**

**Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/mythical/bootstrap`, admin only.

## See where each issue is

**GUI**

**Available now.** Select **History**, or enter `/history.show`. Each issue shows its step, checks, failures, and pull request; each change shows whether it has landed. Open its run or pull request for the detail.

- `/history.backfill` adds the repository's open issues.
- `/history.parallel 3` works on up to three issues at once (1 to 8).
- `/history.retry` retries a blocked or rejected issue.

**TUI**

**Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.**

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/mythical` | The history and every issue on it. |
| `GET .../mythical/events` | A live stream of changes. |
| `POST .../mythical/backfill` | Add open issues. |
| `PUT .../mythical/config` | Set `maxParallel` (admin). |
| `POST .../mythical/items/{id}/retry` | Retry one issue. |

## When is it landed

On a repository that sends work upstream, including Smithers itself, the owner merges the pull request on GitHub. The issue is landed once that commit is on main.

# Run a flow
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/run-a-flow/

A flow is a repeatable job the repository defines: review a change, triage an issue, draft release notes. Each time it runs is a run.

## Pick a flow

**GUI**

**Available now.** Open the repository home and read **Try first**, or type `/` and the flow's name.

![The slash menu finds the review flow declared by the Smithers repository.](/images/app/slash.png)

Finding a flow from the message box.

**TUI**

**Available now.** `/flows` lists the project's flows. They also appear in the `/` menu.

**CLI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs flow list
smthrs flow show review
```

**API**

**Available now.** `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/workflows` lists a repository's flows.

The Smithers repository offers these:

| Flow | Job |
| --- | --- |
| `/review` | Review the working-copy change and explain the verdict. |
| `/lint` | Check named files against the repository's conventions and fix findings. |
| `/pr-triage` | Triage a GitHub pull request from its diff. |
| `/issue-triage` | Reproduce and triage a GitHub issue. |
| `/release-notes` | Draft release notes from the commits since the last tag. |

## Run it

**GUI**

**Available now.** Select the flow and fill in its form: the issue, files, or change to work on. Approve its permissions when asked. A toast follows the run until it finishes; the run card holds the detail. Keep chatting meanwhile.

Needs sign-in and a [box](/docs/learn/boxes/) for the repository.

**TUI**

**Available now.**

```text
/flow review
/flow echo text=hello
```

Quote values with spaces: `text="hello world"`. A missing input opens a form: Tab moves between fields, Space toggles, Enter runs. Esc closes it and leaves the run waiting; press `a` in its tab to reopen. Each run gets its own tab; `/smithers` lists them.

![Filling in a flow's input form in the TUI.](/images/learn/tui-flow-form.gif)

The TUI with fixture flows.

![Running a flow from the TUI and reading its result in the run tab.](/images/learn/tui-run-flow.gif)

The TUI with fixture flows.

**CLI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs flow start review --data '{"args":"Review the working copy"}'
```

Add `--detached` to return as soon as the run is admitted.

**API**

**Available now.**

```sh
curl -X POST "$SMITHERS_API/api/repos/acme/app/invoke" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMITHERS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"flow":"review","input":{"args":"Review main"}}'
```

The response carries the `run_id`.

## Make your own

Ask Smithers to write a flow for a job you repeat, then review it like any code change. To write one yourself, see [Configure an agent and a trigger](/docs/learn/agent-and-trigger/) or [Markdown flows](/docs/guides/markdown-flows/).

# Configure an agent and a trigger
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/agent-and-trigger/

An agent is a file in your repository. A trigger starts it.

## Write the agent

**Available now.** Every surface reads the same file. Create `flows/reviewer/flow.mdx`:

```markdown title="flows/reviewer/flow.mdx"
---
description: Reviews the working-copy change and returns a verdict with reasons.
model: openai:gpt-6-sol
capabilities: ["fs:read:**", "proc:spawn:*"]
budget:
  tokens: 200000
  milliseconds: 600000
---

# Review the change

Read the diff and run the tests. Return approve or request changes,
with the evidence for each finding.
```

Allow only what the job needs. [flow.mdx frontmatter](/docs/reference/flow-mdx/) lists every key. On Smithers Cloud, commit it to the default branch.

## Run it once

Run it like any flow: `/reviewer` in the app, `/agent reviewer` in the TUI, or `smthrs flow start reviewer`. See [Run a flow](/docs/learn/run-a-flow/).

## Put it on a schedule

**GUI**

**Available now.**

1. On the home, open **Run it every night**, or select **Dispatcher** in the sidebar and then **Register a rule**.
2. Pick the flow and select **Schedule**. It runs nightly (02:00 UTC) under the flow's name; a toast follows the registration until it is live.
3. For another schedule, a name, input or limits, type the line instead: `/triggers.register --flow lint --schedule "0 9 * * 1-5"`. That path prepares the plan for you to read and approve before it registers.

Each live schedule has **Run now** and **Pause**. A scheduled run needs a token and time budget; the form uses the flow's `budget`.

![The Dispatcher lists a repository's rules and the flows they start, with a Register a rule button.](/images/app/dispatcher.png)

The Dispatcher card.

**TUI**

**Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Available now** for a local project:

```sh
smthrs triggers register weekday-review --flow reviewer --cron "0 9 * * 1-5" --timezone America/New_York
smthrs triggers list
smthrs triggers fire weekday-review
```

Keep `smthrs serve` running for schedules to fire. A fired run still asks for approval. See [Define triggers](/docs/guides/triggers/).

**API**

**Partly available.** `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/repository-jobs` lists registrations, and `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/repository-jobs/{job}/pause` pauses one. Registering one over the API is planned.

## Keep the rule with the code

**Partly available.** To keep rules with the code, add them to `.smithers/FACTORY.ts`. When main moves, rules for `flow.mdx` agents go live; rules for `flow.ts` flows stay declared only. See [Triggers and flows](/docs/how-it-works/triggers-and-flows/#rules).

```ts title=".smithers/FACTORY.ts"
import { Smithers as S } from "@smthrs/targets"

export const factory = S.Factory({
  summary: "How this repository develops itself.",
  on: {
    "schedule:0 9 * * 1-5": { flow: "reviewer", description: "Weekday morning review" }
  }
})
```

- [Agents](/docs/how-it-works/agents/): the idea behind agents.

# Work in the background
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/background-work/

Give a job a clear result and a small set of files. It runs in the background while you keep chatting.

```text
Fix the failing search tests. Keep changes inside src/search.ts and its tests.
```

## Hand it off

**GUI**

**Available now.** Ask in chat, or start a flow. A toast follows the work until it finishes; the run card holds the detail. Chat stays usable.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Ask in chat. Smithers starts a worker in its own tab and returns to chat. Up to six run at once (`SMITHERS_TUI_WORKERS`); more wait in order.

![A worker runs in its own TUI tab while chat stays available.](/images/learn/tui-background-worker.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

**CLI**

**Available now.** Start a flow and return as soon as it's admitted:

```sh
smthrs flow start review --data '{"args":"Review main"}' --detached
```

**API**

**Available now.** `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/invoke` returns at once with the `run_id`.

## Follow, stop, retry

| State | Means |
| --- | --- |
| Requested | Saved; not started yet. |
| Queued | Waiting for a free slot. |
| Running | Working. |
| Waiting | Waiting for work it started. |
| Parked | Waiting for provider capacity. |
| Done | Finished; read the result and checks. |
| Failed | Read the error, then retry. |
| Cancelled | Stopped. |

**GUI**

**Available now.** The toast offers the controls that apply; the run card has **Steer** and **Stop**. See [Watch an agent work](/docs/learn/watch-an-agent/#steer-or-stop).

**TUI**

**Available now.** Open a worker with `/tabs` or Ctrl+]. In its tab: `s` steers, `c` opens it in chat, `x` stops, `r` retries with its earlier steps, `m` picks another model, `w` waits for the provider's reset. `/stop <id>` and `/retry <id>` work from anywhere.

![Stopping and retrying a worker from its TUI tab.](/images/learn/tui-worker-controls.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

A worker can start its own workers, three levels deep. A `tree:` tab shows them together.

![A lead worker with a child worker in a TUI tree tab.](/images/learn/tui-worker-tree.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

**CLI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs runs list --status running
smthrs runs cancel <run>
smthrs runs resume <run>
```

**API**

**Available now.** API procedures `List`, `Cancel`, and `Resume`; see [HTTP and RPC endpoints](/docs/reference/http-api/).

# Choose a model
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/models/

Each agent names its model in its file (`model:`). You can also pick the model for chat and override it per run.

## Pick a model

**GUI**

**Available now.** `/model.list` shows the models and which one each job uses. `/model.assign` changes one.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Ctrl+L or `/model` opens the picker; type to filter. Ctrl+P and Ctrl+Shift+P step through models. `/model provider:modelId` picks one directly.

![Filtering and choosing a model in the TUI picker.](/images/learn/tui-model-picker.gif)

The TUI with placeholder provider keys.

| Setting | Applies to |
| --- | --- |
| `--model provider:modelId` | Chat |
| `SMITHERS_TUI_SEAT` | Default chat model |
| `SMITHERS_TUI_WORKER_SEAT` | Default background model |
| `SMITHERS_TUI_WORKER_SEATS=a,b` | Fallbacks when a provider is at its limit |
| An agent's `model:` | That agent |

**CLI**

**Available now.** Set it in the flow's `model:` line. For one answer:

```sh
smthrs tui -p "Explain this repository." --model openai:gpt-6-sol
```

`smthrs doctor` lists the provider keys it found.

**API**

**Available now.** The flow's `model:` line decides; there is no per-request override.

## Reasoning effort

**GUI**

**Available now.** Set `effort:` in the agent's file.

**TUI**

**Available now.** `/thinking` takes `default`, `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `xhigh`. Shift+Tab cycles through them.

**CLI**

**Available now.** Set `effort:` in the agent's file.

**API**

**Available now.** Set `effort:` in the agent's file.

Support varies by provider. See [Configure models and providers](/docs/guides/model-seats/) for providers and keys.

# Watch an agent work
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/watch-an-agent/

An agent's history is its runs. Each run has a timeline.

## Flags to look for

| Flag | Means |
| --- | --- |
| Thrashing | The agent repeats work without progress. |
| Blocked | The run paused and needs a resume. |
| Approval needed | The run waits for your decision. |
| Runaway | A budget or time limit paused it. Planned. |

## Find an agent's runs

**GUI**

**Available now.** Select **Agents** in the sidebar, then **Runs** beside an agent. Or enter `/runs.list` with **Flow** set to the agent's id, such as `reviewer`. Select a run to open it.

![The Agents card lists each agent with its model and a Runs button.](/images/learn/app-agents.png)

The Agents card.

**Partly available.** The card lists the built-in agents; your own agents appear once [#2113](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2113) lands.

**TUI**

**Available now.** `/smithers` lists flow runs, newest first. Select one to open its tab. Background workers each have a tab too; see [Work in the background](/docs/learn/background-work/).

**CLI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs runs list --flow reviewer
smthrs runs list --status waiting-approval
```

**API**

**Available now.** API procedure `List { _tag: "runs", filters: { flowId: "reviewer" } }`. Over HTTP, `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/workflows/{id}/runs` lists one flow's runs.

## Read the timeline

**GUI**

**Available now.** The run card shows the trace as a tree and a timeline, with the flags above. Select a row for its inputs, output, and token use. Filter the trace, or select **Maximize card** for room.

![A run card with status, trace filters, a call tree, and controls to stop or steer the run.](/images/app/run-example.png)

A run card, with example data.

**Available now.** Select **Steps** for one row per step: time, type, description, duration, and tokens. Select a step for its detail. **Partly available:** the first row names what started the run only for code pushes so far ([#2115](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2115)).

![The Steps view: a run flagged Runaway, with a Resume button and five steps with durations and tokens.](/images/learn/preview-run-steps.png)

The Steps view, with example data.

**TUI**

**Available now.** The timeline sits above the composer, with phases (Researching, Implementing, Testing, Stuck, Blocked) and milestones. Press Ctrl+T to inspect it; arrows move, `[` and `]` jump between milestones, Home and End jump to the ends, Esc returns to live. An earlier point shows only what was known then.

![Scrubbing the TUI timeline across phases and milestones.](/images/learn/tui-timeline.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

**CLI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs runs show <run>
smthrs runs logs <run> --follow
```

`show` gives the status and a diagnosis. `logs` streams events as they commit.

**API**

**Available now.** API procedure `Watch { runId, follow: true }` streams events. `Projection.Snapshot` with selector `run-events` or `run-tree` returns the recorded trace.

## Steer or stop

**GUI**

**Available now.** Type a correction in the run's steering box and select **Steer**. Use **Stop** to cancel it. For a paused run, enter `/runs.resume`. Starting it again creates a second run.

```text
Keep the existing public API. Fix the parser and add a regression test.
```

**TUI**

**Available now.** In a flow run's tab, `x` stops it and `r` resumes it. `/stop <id>` and `/retry <id>` do the same by ID.

**CLI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs runs steer <run> --message "Keep the existing public API."
smthrs runs cancel <run>
smthrs runs resume <run>
```

**API**

**Available now.** API procedures `Steer { runId, message, idempotencyKey }`, `Cancel`, and `Resume`. Over HTTP, `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/runs/{id}/cancel` and `/resume`.

If the run waits on a decision, [answer the approval](/docs/learn/approvals/). If it failed, read its error before retrying. If it produced a change, [review it](/docs/learn/review-a-change/).

## Next

- [Answer an approval](/docs/learn/approvals/): unblock a waiting run.
- [Review a change](/docs/learn/review-a-change/): read the result.

# Answer an approval
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/approvals/

Some steps wait for you: a file edit, a command, a launch. The run pauses until you decide. Read what it asks, then approve or deny.

## Find what's waiting

**GUI**

**Available now.** An approval card appears in the conversation. To list every pending request on the repository, enter `/approvals.list`. Each request names its run; open the run for context.

**Available now.** **Inbox** in the sidebar opens the same list. **Planned:** runs a budget or time guard paused, with **Continue** and **Stop** ([#2114](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2114)).

![Design preview of the Inbox: a paused run with Continue and Stop, an approval, and a question.](/images/learn/preview-inbox.png)

Design preview with example data. Not connected yet.

**TUI**

**Available now.** The request appears above the composer. Start the TUI with `--approve ask` to be asked, or `--approve deny` to refuse every call; the default allows every call. `SMITHERS_TUI_APPROVE` sets the same.

```sh
smthrs tui --approve ask
```

**Planned.** A list of pending approvals across runs ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs approvals list
```

Each entry carries the exact payload to approve. With nothing waiting, it prints `[]`.

**API**

**Available now**, over the gateway's projection RPC: `Projection.Snapshot` with selector `{ _tag: "approvals" }`. Each row has `runId`, `requestId`, `title`, `payload`, and `status`. See [HTTP and RPC endpoints](/docs/reference/http-api/).

## Decide

**GUI**

**Available now.**

1. Read the requested action and the repository or run it concerns.
2. Check that it matches the work you asked for.
3. Select **Approve** or **Deny**, and wait for the card to show your decision.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Press `y` to allow once or `n` to deny. Where offered, `a` allows that kind of call for the rest of the conversation. The keys work once the editor is empty. A flow asks once for each thing it may do.

![A flow asks for its write, process, and network permissions in turn; pressing y allows each, and the run completes.](/images/learn/tui-flow-approval.gif)

The TUI with a fixture flow.

**CLI**

**Available now.** Pass the payload from `approvals list`, or `@file`:

```sh
smthrs approvals approve @approval.json
smthrs approvals deny @approval.json
```

`--scope once|run|remembered` sets how far an approval reaches. The default is `run`.

**API**

**Available now.** `Approval.Submit { target, scope, idempotencyKey, decision: "approve" | "deny" }` over the API. See [HTTP and RPC endpoints](/docs/reference/http-api/).

## Correct it instead

If the request is too broad or targets the wrong repository, deny it and tell Smithers what to change. For a running flow, [steer the run](/docs/learn/watch-an-agent/#steer-or-stop).

## Next

- [Watch an agent work](/docs/learn/watch-an-agent/): see why a run paused.
- [Review a change](/docs/learn/review-a-change/): check the result before it lands.

# Review a change
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/review-a-change/

A change is the code a run proposes, with the evidence for landing it.

## Read the diff

**GUI**

**Available now.** Open the change from the run's result, or enter `/change.view <id>`. Start with **Diff**; select **Full diff** for every line. With several revisions, compare them with the revision selectors.

![A change card with its revision, changed files, review views, and landing controls.](/images/app/change-example.png)

A change card, with example data.

**TUI**

**Available now** for edits the TUI made locally. Press Ctrl+S for **Summary**. Pick a row with the arrows, Enter expands it, `d` shows its diff, `v` switches split and unified.

![Reading a captured edit's diff in the TUI Summary.](/images/learn/tui-review-diff.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/changes/{id}` and `/changes/{id}/diff`.

## Check the evidence

**GUI**

**Available now.** **Checks** shows check results, **Findings** shows analyzer findings, and **Review** shows verdicts and discussion. Ask Smithers to fix a specific finding, then read the new diff and checks.

![The Checks view of a change card with a build result.](/images/app/checks-example.png)

Checks, with example data.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Expand a command row in **Summary** to read its output.

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/changes/{id}/findings`; reviews and comments live on the landing: `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/landings/{number}/reviews`.

## Land it, or undo it

**GUI**

**Available now.** When checks and required reviews pass, select **Land**. Its label shows the range, such as **Land 1 → 2**; check it before confirming. If landing is blocked, the card says what's missing.

On a repository that sends work upstream, including Smithers itself, landing opens a GitHub pull request for the owner to merge.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Changes stay in your checkout; commit them yourself. To undo one, select its row in **Summary** and press `u`. Undo refuses if the file changed since, or if a shell command made the change.

![Undoing a captured edit from the TUI Summary.](/images/learn/tui-undo-edit.gif)

The TUI with a scripted test model.

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** `PUT /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/landings/{number}/land`.

- [Follow an issue to main](/docs/learn/issue-to-main/): where each change is.

# Use the wiki
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/wiki/

The wiki holds what people and agents know about the project. Every edit is a revision.

## Read and edit

**GUI**

**Available now.**

1. Select **Wiki** in the sidebar and choose a page.
2. Edit it in place, or select **New note**. Keep each fact with its source.
3. Close the pane to return to the conversation.

With no pages yet, **Create Wiki** generates them.

![The Wiki card for a repository with no pages yet, with a Create Wiki button.](/images/app/wiki.png)

The Wiki card before any pages exist.

**TUI**

**Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now** where the host enables the Wiki service.

```sh
curl "$SMITHERS_API/api/repos/acme/app/wiki" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMITHERS_TOKEN"
curl "$SMITHERS_API/api/repos/acme/app/wiki/getting-started" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMITHERS_TOKEN"
curl -X PATCH "$SMITHERS_API/api/repos/acme/app/wiki/getting-started" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMITHERS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"expected_revision":3,"body":"# Getting started\n\nRun pnpm install."}'
```

`expected_revision` refuses the edit if someone saved first. `GET .../wiki/{slug}/revisions` lists history.

## Generate pages from the code

**GUI**

**Available now.** Enter `/wiki.create owner/repo`. Smithers writes the pages declared in `.smithers/coding-project.json`, in the background. `/wiki.cloud owner/repo` browses the published pages. The repository needs its [stack](/docs/learn/issue-to-main/) turned on.

**TUI**

**Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/mythical/wiki` requests a refresh and answers `202`. It answers `409` if the stack is off or the repository declares no wiki.

## Kept current

**Partly available.** When main moves, Smithers regenerates the declared pages, reviews them against the code, and keeps pages a person edited. Hosted proof is tracked in [#1923](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1923).

The single `coding/wiki` generator uses `.smithers/coding-project.json`. Refreshes retain source and review receipts; unchanged pages can reuse reviews across host deployments ([#1971](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1971)). A requested refresh is not a completed refresh.

## Markdown spaces and sync

**Backend available; app connection pending** ([#1922](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1922)). Pass `?visibility=public|private` on every wiki API request. Public pages follow repository visibility; private pages require explicit repository access. Markdown paths, YAML frontmatter, wikilinks, backlinks, tags, folders and versioned attachments share the existing page history.

**Planned.** Two-way sync with Notion or a Markdown folder depends on the shared sync mechanism ([#2122](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2122)). No existing vault is imported automatically.

## Next

- [Wiki](/docs/how-it-works/wiki/): the idea behind this page.

# Open a repository
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/open-a-repository/

A repository gives your conversation its context: files, flows, issues, and wiki.

## Open one

**GUI**

**Available now.** On [smithers.sh](https://smithers.sh), pick a repository and select **Open Smithers**. Its home shows the description and featured flows. With several repositories, switch with the selector beside the message box.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Start it in the checkout: `smthrs tui /path/to/repo`.

**CLI**

**Available now.** From a checkout, open it in the app:

```sh
smthrs open
```

It opens the desktop app when installed, otherwise prints the `https://smithers.sh/<owner>/<repo>` link.

**API**

**Available now.** `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}`; `GET /api/user/repos` lists yours.

## Read its guide files

**GUI**

**Available now.** Enter `/files.read README.md` or `/files.read CONTRIBUTING.md`. Select **Maximize card** for more room.

![CONTRIBUTING.md open in a file card.](/images/app/file.png)

A file card.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Ask for it, or type `@README.md` to add it to your message.

**CLI**

Read the files in your checkout.

**API**

**Available now.** `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/file/{change_id}/{path}`.

## Register your repository

Register a repository; we review it. You can register one at a time.

Paste the repository's link. Smithers analyzes it while you watch, answering each question itself, and gives you a report: license, how checks run, contributors, agent readiness, and chores worth automating. The report is yours to keep. Then we review the registration and set Smithers up.

**GUI**

**Planned.** Sign in with GitHub on [smithers.sh](https://smithers.sh/smithersai/smithers), then select **Register a repository** on [the home page](https://smithers.sh/?register=1), or enter `/repository.register`. Paste the link. Smithers' own choices animate as it makes them. A row in the sidebar shows where it is: Analyzing, In review, Setting up, Ready.

**TUI**

Not applicable: start the TUI in any checkout.

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Planned.**

# Work in a box
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/boxes/

A box is where Smithers works on a repository in the cloud: the working copy, terminals, agents at work, and services.

## Open a box

**GUI**

**Available now.** Select the repository, enter `/box.open`, fill in the bookmark if asked, and approve. Opening can reuse the box for that bookmark. Wait for it to report ready.

**TUI**

The TUI works in your local checkout; it doesn't use boxes. Hosted boxes in the TUI are **Planned** ([#2119](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/2119)).

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/workspaces` creates one; `GET .../workspaces` lists them.

## Files and terminal

**GUI**

**Available now.** Expand the box under its repository in the sidebar and select a file to open it. Open the box card for its terminal, services, and network activity.

![A box card with its views and controls to suspend or delete it.](/images/app/box-example.png)

A box card, with example data.

**TUI**

Not applicable: the TUI edits your local files and runs commands with `!`.

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** `GET .../workspaces/{id}/files` and `/files/content`; the terminal is a WebSocket at `.../workspace/sessions/{id}/terminal`.

## Suspend, resume, delete

**GUI**

**Available now.** **Suspend** stops a box and keeps it; **Resume** brings it back. Deleting asks you to confirm the box's name.

**TUI**

Not applicable.

**CLI**

**Planned** ([#1989](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/1989)).

**API**

**Available now.** `POST .../workspaces/{id}/suspend`, `POST .../workspaces/{id}/resume`, `DELETE .../workspaces/{id}`. `POST .../workspaces/{id}/snapshot` saves a point; `POST .../workspaces/{id}/fork` starts a new box from it.

# Search
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/search/

Search when you know what you want but not where it is.

## Find anything

**GUI**

| Prefix | Finds |
| --- | --- |
| none | Everything, by name |
| `/` | Flows and commands |
| `//` | Build targets |
| `wiki:` | Wiki pages |
| `run:` | Runs |
| `change:` | Changes |
| `#` | Issues |
| `box:` | Boxes |
| `secret:` | Secret names |

![The search palette listing its prefixes after typing a question mark.](/images/app/search.png)

Search prefixes.

**TUI**

**Available now.** Press Ctrl+K. Type `@` in the composer to mention a file.

| Input | Finds | Enter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `math` | Commands and file paths | Runs it, or inserts `@path` |
| `/` | Commands | Runs it |
| `text:add` | Text in files | Inserts `@path:line` |
| `conversation:review` | Saved conversations | Resumes it |
| `tab:review` | Background workers | Opens it |

# Repository secrets
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/secrets/

Everything that runs in a repository's boxes may use its secrets. Values are never shown. Never paste a secret into chat.

## See the list

**GUI**

**Available now.** Select **Secrets** in the sidebar. Each row shows the name, the hosts it is bound to, the header it sets, and when it changed.

**TUI**

The TUI reads secrets from your local environment. See [Configuration](/docs/tui/configuration/).

**CLI**

**Available now** for local credentials, stored encrypted in the project:

```sh
smthrs credentials list
```

**API**

**Available now.** `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/secrets`, with write permission.

## Add or remove one

**GUI**

**Planned.** Adding and removing secrets in the app. Ask a repository admin to use the API meanwhile.

**TUI**

Set the variable in your shell before starting the TUI.

**CLI**

**Available now** for local credentials:

```sh
export SMITHERS_CREDENTIAL_KEY=<your key>
smthrs credentials add github --name "GitHub" --secret-env GITHUB_TOKEN
smthrs credentials revoke github
```

**API**

**Available now**, admin only. `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/secrets` adds one; `DELETE /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/secrets/{name}` removes it.

# Troubleshooting
https://smithers.sh/docs/learn/troubleshooting/

Start with the error on the card, row, or output. It names what failed and what to do next.

## Find the error

**GUI**

**Available now.** Read the card or notification. Open the run card for its status, output, and any waiting approval.

| You see | Do |
| --- | --- |
| A sign-in prompt | Sign in with GitHub. |
| Your repository isn't there | [Register it](/docs/learn/open-a-repository/#register-your-repository); we review it. |
| No flows or boxes | Check the selected repository, then [open a box](/docs/learn/boxes/). |
| A notification over a control | Select **Dismiss**, then retry. |
| An unknown slash command | Type `/` and pick from the menu. |
| An empty Wiki or History | [Generate the wiki](/docs/learn/wiki/) or [turn on the stack](/docs/learn/issue-to-main/). |
| A waiting or failed run | [Answer its approval](/docs/learn/approvals/), or fix the error and retry. |

**TUI**

**Available now.** Ctrl+O expands a row's error; `/conversation` shows the log path.

| You see | Do |
| --- | --- |
| No model available | Set a provider key and restart. See [Configuration](/docs/tui/configuration/). |
| Worker parked | Wait for its reset, or press `m` for another model. |
| Worker failed | Press `r` to retry. |
| `Stop running work first` | Stop or finish running work before switching conversations or undoing. |
| Undo refused | The file changed since; review the newer edit. |
| Flow runs old code | Restart the TUI after changing a `flow.ts`. |
| Input form gone | Open the flow's tab and press `a`. |
| `y` types a letter | Empty the editor and wait for the approval keys. |
| Monitor refused | Set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`. |

![A provider refusal in the TUI with its error expanded.](/images/learn/tui-provider-failure.gif)

The TUI with a refusing test provider.

**CLI**

**Available now.**

```sh
smthrs doctor
smthrs info
```

`doctor` checks flow discovery, providers, tools, and stored state. `info` reports the workspace and host.

**API**

**Available now.** An error response carries `code` and `message`, and an `X-Request-Id` header. `retry_after` or `Retry-After` says when to retry.

## Report a problem

Check [Smithers status](https://status.smithers.sh). Then open an issue in the [Smithers repository](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues) with what you did, the error, the repository, and the run ID. Remove credentials and private code first.

**GUI**

Include a screenshot with private details removed.

**TUI**

Include the command, runtime version, and a redacted excerpt of the conversation log.

**CLI**

**Available now.** Submit a redacted report:

```sh
smthrs bug "flow start hangs after approval" --dry-run
```

**API**

Include the request, status, response body, and `X-Request-Id`, without the token.

# Smithers in your terminal
https://smithers.sh/docs/tui/

`smthrs tui` is Smithers in a terminal. It works in your local checkout: ask for a change, keep chatting while it works, and inspect every step. The tutorials show it in each **TUI** tab.

## Try it in a browser

The [playground](https://tui.smithers.sh) runs the same agent on a two-file sandbox, with no access to your computer. Move the checkpoint slider to see the files at any step, and branch to try another approach.

## Install

Until the release is published, run it from a source checkout. You need the Node version in `.node-version`, pnpm 11.25.0, Bun 1.4 or later, jj 0.39.0 or later, ripgrep, and the Rust toolchain `rust-toolchain.toml` pins.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/smithersai/smithers.git
cd smithers
pnpm install
cargo build --locked --release -p smithers-ffi --bin smithers-jj-export
bun run tui /path/to/project
```

Set a provider key first, such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`. `smthrs tui` takes the same arguments once installed. On Alpine, the compiled binary also needs `apk add libstdc++`.

## Make a first change

Give it a check it can run:

```text
Fix math.js so node check.mjs passes.
```

![The TUI fixes a subtraction bug in math.js and runs the check until it passes.](/images/learn/tui-fix-add.gif)

The TUI replaying a recorded model run.

Press Ctrl+S for **Summary**: each edit with its diff, each command with its output.

## Editor and mouse

Ctrl+A/Ctrl+E move to the beginning/end of a line. Ctrl+W deletes a word and Ctrl+U deletes to the start of the line. Ctrl+K belongs to search. Drag text to copy a selection; click tabs, worker rows, cards, or status actions to open/invoke them. Scroll with the mouse or PageUp/PageDown.

Ctrl+C clears the editor; twice within 500 ms exits. Ctrl+D exits only with an empty editor. Approval letters arm only after the editor is empty and their 400 ms guard has elapsed.

Repository and runtime [extensions](/docs/tui/extend/) add keys under their owner in the popup. Built-in keys and text-editing bindings cannot be shadowed.

# Command line
https://smithers.sh/docs/tui/cli/

```text
smthrs tui [directory] [--model provider:modelId] [-c | -r] [-p "prompt"] [--approve all|ask|deny]
```

From a source checkout, use `bun run tui` with the same arguments.

| Option | Short | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `directory` | | Working directory; defaults to the current one. |
| `--model provider:modelId` | `-m` | Chat model; overrides `SMITHERS_TUI_SEAT`. |
| `--continue` | `-c` | Continue the latest conversation in this directory. |
| `--resume` | `-r` | Pick a conversation to continue. |
| `--print "prompt"` | `-p` | Answer one prompt, print it, and exit. |
| `--approve all` | | Run edits, commands, and network calls. The default. |
| `--approve ask` | | Ask first. Interactive only. |
| `--approve deny` | | Refuse them. |
| `--help` | `-h` | Show options. |

## One answer

```bash
smthrs tui /path/to/project -p "Explain how the search index is built."
```

Exits 0 on an answer and 1 on failure or cancellation. `--approve ask` is refused in this mode.

![The TUI prints one answer and exits.](/images/learn/tui-print-mode.gif)

Print mode with a scripted test model.

## Runtime

`smthrs tui` tries `SMITHERS_TUI_BIN`, an installed binary, Bun, then Node 26.4 or later. Interactive compiled builds need a writable, executable `TMPDIR`.

```bash
cargo build --locked --release -p smithers-ffi --bin smithers-jj-export
node packages/smithers/scripts/build-tui.mjs
SMITHERS_WORKSPACE_JJ_EXPORT_BINARY="$PWD/target/release/smithers-jj-export" \
  node --experimental-ffi --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning packages/smithers/dist/tui/main.js /path/to/project
```

## Exit

`/quit` or `/exit`. Ctrl+D exits with an empty editor; Ctrl+C twice within 500 ms exits. Stop background work with its own controls first.
